chunks: From him, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who loses consciousness and then regains it. He said: 'He must make up what he missed; he should give the adhan for the first [prayer] and call the iqamah for the remainder.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up prayers after losing consciousness?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific legal ruling for a worshipper who loses consciousness mid-prayer is clarified: they must perform the adhan for the first prayer unit and the iqamah for the remainder, ensuring the ritual structure is maintained upon recovery. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of prayer obligations even during states of temporary incapacitation, distinguishing it from complete nullification. It reflects the practical application of fiqh principles regarding the validity of actions performed with partial consciousness.
